```{r}
#| label: setup
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
source(file.path("..", "Figure_Data", "FigureABM.R"))

ASSUMPTIONS <- c(
  baseline = "Baseline",
  "78pct"  = "78%",
  "86pct"  = "86%",
  "93pct"  = "93%"
)
ADULTS <- c("18to24", "25to44", "45to69", "70+")
GROUPS <- c("Total", "Children", "Adults")

fmt <- function(x) formatC(round(x), format = "d", big.mark = ",")
```

```{r}
#| label: data
# Final infections per run, by age, of the three Figure 4 arms
runs <- rbindlist(lapply(names(ASSUMPTIONS), function(v) {
  rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(FOCAL_SCENARIOS)), function(i) {
    s <- FOCAL_SCENARIOS[i]
    f <- scenario_file(".", 9, s$rash, s$ct, vax_adults = v)
    x <- as.data.table(
      readRDS(f)[[sub("outbreak_size", "infections_by_age", s$arm)]]
    )
    x[,
      .(
        Children = as.numeric(sum(infections[!age_group %in% ADULTS])),
        Adults   = as.numeric(sum(infections[age_group %in% ADULTS]))
      ),
      by = sim_num
    ][, `:=`(Total = Children + Adults, model = s$label, vax_adults = v)]
  }))
}))

retained <- runs[Total >= MIN_OUTBREAK_SIZE]

sizes <- melt(
  retained,
  id.vars       = c("vax_adults", "model"),
  measure.vars  = GROUPS,
  variable.name = "group"
)[,
  .(
    median = median(value),
    q025   = quantile(value, 0.025, names = FALSE),
    q25    = quantile(value, 0.25, names = FALSE),
    q75    = quantile(value, 0.75, names = FALSE),
    q975   = quantile(value, 0.975, names = FALSE)
  ),
  by = .(vax_adults, model, group)
]

sizes[, vax_adults := factor(vax_adults, names(ASSUMPTIONS), ASSUMPTIONS)]
sizes[, model := factor(model, FOCAL_SCENARIOS$label)]
sizes[, group := factor(group, GROUPS)]
```

The three focal scenarios of Figure 4 at R0 = 9 (`make population_immunity`), for each assumption on the vaccination coverage of adults aged 18 to 69: the current one (`baseline`) and the alternate adult immunization assumptions of the [`multigroup.vaccine` vignette](https://epiforesite.github.io/multigroup-vaccine/articles/experiments/utaz_age_school.html), with 78%, 86%, and 93% coverage. Each scenario has 1,000 runs; runs with fewer than `r MIN_OUTBREAK_SIZE` cases are excluded as early extinctions. As in Figure 4, self-isolation with quarantine uses the run with quarantine and the other two scenarios the run without. Children are those under 18.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-population-immunity
cells <- dcast(
  sizes[, .(
    vax_adults, model, group,
    value = sprintf("%s (%s-%s)", fmt(median), fmt(q25), fmt(q75))
  )],
  vax_adults + model ~ group,
  value.var = "value"
)
ratio <- dcast(sizes, vax_adults + model ~ group, value.var = "median")[,
  .(vax_adults, model, ratio = sprintf("%.1f", Children / Adults))
]
n_retained <- retained[, .(retained = fmt(.N)), by = .(vax_adults, model)]
n_retained[, `:=`(
  vax_adults = factor(vax_adults, names(ASSUMPTIONS), ASSUMPTIONS),
  model      = factor(model, levels(sizes$model))
)]

tab <- n_retained[
  cells[ratio, on = .(vax_adults, model)],
  on = .(vax_adults, model)
]
setorder(tab, vax_adults, model)

kable(
  tab[, .(
    vax_adults, model,
    retained,
    Total, Children, Adults, ratio
  )],
  col.names = c(
    "Adult vaccination", "Scenario", "Retained runs",
    "Total infections", "Children", "Adults", "Child:adult ratio"
  ),
  align     = "llrrrrr",
  caption   = paste(
    "Final outbreak size at day 365, median (interquartile range) across",
    "the retained runs; the ratio is of the medians."
  )
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-population-immunity
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "Figure SI 11. Projected final outbreak size at R0 = 9 under alternative adult vaccination-coverage assumptions. Simulations used the baseline coverage and 78%, 86%, and 93% coverage among adults aged 18-69 years, under no interventions, self-isolation only, and self-isolation with quarantine. Panels show total infections, infections among children younger than 18 years, and infections among adults aged 18 years or older. Points denote the median at day 365 across simulations with at least 10 cases; vertical bars denote the 95% interval (2.5th to 97.5th percentiles) across those simulations."
dodge <- position_dodge(width = 0.3)

ggplot(sizes, aes(vax_adults, median, color = model, group = model)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.5, position = dodge) +
  geom_pointrange(
    aes(ymin = q025, ymax = q975),
    size      = 0.3,
    linewidth = 0.6,
    position  = dodge
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~group,
    nrow     = 1,
    labeller = as_labeller(c(
      Total    = "Total",
      Children = "Children (under 18)",
      Adults   = "Adults (18+)"
    ))
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = SCENARIO_COLORS) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = fmt, limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(x = "Adult vaccination coverage (ages 18-69)", y = "Infections") +
  theme_figure4() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", color = INK_PRIMARY))
```
